name: video-ambient

frames.best_why: The video sits centred with the full blue halo bleeding on every side and the glow toggle readable below.

tagline: A video whose colours spill past its edges as a glowing halo.
summary: A rounded video player samples its own frames into a soft halo that bleeds past its borders, with a small toggle that switches the ambient glow off to compare.
appearance: A rounded rectangular video of a green mossy stone floating on blue water, with a blue to teal glow spreading well past its edges. A small dark pill beneath reads Ambient glow: On.
behaviour: The video plays on a loop and its dominant colours are resampled several times a second, so the halo shifts with the footage. The small button below toggles the glow on and off.
demo_content: Aerial footage of a green mossy stone on blue water; the button reads Ambient glow: On
search_phrases: video with glow around the edges
colours bleed out of the video
use_when: A hero or showcase wants a video to feel like a lit screen rather than a flat rectangle.
avoid_when: When a fixed brand colour is required, since the halo takes its hue from the footage and shifts as it plays.
customise: src, alt, poster and playback flags are props, plus glow, intensity, scale, blur, saturation, gain and sample rate for the halo. Colours come from the footage itself.
weight_why: Two tiny canvas grabs per sample plus heavy blur filters; it idles when paused.

a11y.note: Muted autoplay video is labelled and reduced motion stops it, but controls default off so keyboard users cannot pause it.

issues: With controls off by default there is no visible way to pause the looping footage.
polish_why: The halo tracks the footage convincingly and the toggle proves it; no pause control holds it back.
